links.outcome: LLM exam accuracy with versus without retrieval-augmented grounding in a radiotherapy knowledge database
links.effect: Accuracy rose from 77.0% to 84.6% (Medical Physicist), 74.9% to 82.1% (Radiologist), and 55.6% to 71.7% (Radiation Oncologist); gains ranged from 7.2% to 16.1%.
links.quote: Accuracy increased from 77.0% ± 2.6% to 84.6% ± 1.5% in the Medical Physicist examination, from 74.9% ± 2.0% to 82.1% ± 1.1% in the Radiologist examination, and from 55.6% ± 4.4% to 71.7% ± 4.5% in the Radiation Oncologist examination.

screen.practice: retrieval grounding (RAG) added to existing LLM
screen.reason: The study directly compares the performance of an existing LLM (ChatGPT-4o) with and without retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) using clinical guidelines/textbooks on Japanese radiotherapy board examinations.
